- When sentiment is strongly positive (≥ 0.67) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next period.  
- When sentiment is strongly negative (≤ -0.00) or mixed, model underestimates; adjust upward by 1–3% if recent price is falling.  
- Model consistently underestimates prices after sharp upward spikes (e.g., >5% from prior period); add 2–5% buffer to forecast for such periods.  
- Model shows persistent lag in capturing mean reversion; if 3+ consecutive days show price below 10-day moving average, forecast should be adjusted upward.  
- For 30-day horizon, model often misses late-period price surges (especially after sentiment shifts); increase forecast by 1–3% for last 5–7 days if sentiment turns positive.  
- If sentiment history shows alternating +/– cycles, model tends to misalign with sentiment direction; align forecast slope with sentiment trend direction.
